root_idea.summary: The root is oriented toward the chest or a surface laid upon the ground, with related extensions to a settled place, remaining in a place, and states of clinging or disorientation.
root_idea.development: The central image develops from the chest or something resting on the ground to a bounded land or locality. Further lexical extensions include abiding in a place, traces left upon a surface, bodily spaces, bewilderment, weakness, and dullness.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic noun بلد and its plural بلاد form a distinct public headword.
The Quranic noun بلدة is a distinct feminine lexical form, although its land and locality meanings overlap with بلد.

senses.definition: A bounded inhabited locality or territory: a city, town, country, or region.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form may refer to a particular settled place, including Mecca, or more broadly to a country or region. Its plural بلاد may mean cities, lands, or countries collectively.

senses.definition: A tract of land, especially land described as barren, dead, or desert.
senses.usage_conditions: In the construction بلد ميت, the expression denotes land without productive vegetation; the noun can also be used for a desert or waterless tract.

senses.definition: A bounded tract of land or locality; a land, territory, or city viewed as a particular place.
senses.usage_conditions: The form overlaps with بلد but can specify a particular portion or tract. In Quranic usage it describes land as good, dead, or associated with a city or territory.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain, stay, abide, or dwell in a place, especially one adopted as one's country or residence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may be construed with a place and can carry the sense of keeping to it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To keep to the ground while fighting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of combatants who remain on the ground in battle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have marks or traces remain upon the skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The marks are described as أبلاد in the cited lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A clear space between the eyebrows, or eyebrows that are not joined.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is also used adjectivally of a person having this feature.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become stupid, dull, inert, or lacking in effective intelligence and vigor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb can also describe softness, weakness, or lack of endurance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an animal, to lag behind or fail to show briskness in running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence applies the usage especially to a horse and also to a camel that cannot be made lively by urging.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain or stay, or to cast oneself down upon the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The act of lying down may be attributed to fatigue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become languid or deliberately lazy after having been brisk or lively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a change of vigor or conduct rather than simple residence in a place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be weak or ineffective in work, generosity, or running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage describes inability or deficient performance in the stated activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be niggardly, avaricious, or unwilling to give generously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a characterization of a person's liberality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a cloud, to give no rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is specifically predicated of clouds or a cloud.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fail to apply oneself properly or effectively to anything.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning concerns ineffective application or conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To appear low or shortened in extent because of the darkness of night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is marked as figurative and is applied to mountains or regions as they appear to the observer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Contending with another in combat with swords or staves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun denotes mutual fighting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleave or cling to the ground in submissiveness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may also describe an animal that has become dull and cannot be made brisk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a beast, to become dull and unresponsive to attempts to make it lively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence specifically describes an animal that remains sluggish when put into motion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone keep to a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction takes a person as object and a place as the location to which he is made to adhere.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a watering-trough or tank, to become or be left abandoned, worn, and no longer used, so that it threatens to fall into ruin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The abandonment may be described as resulting from time; the related adjective can also mean old when applied to such a structure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To obtain or exercise dominion over a country or town belonging to others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is a بلد in the sense of a territory or locality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To alight or sojourn in a deserted country or place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited construction evokes a place with no one present.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become confounded or perplexed and unable to see the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense describes going back and forth in confusion, as though lost in a pathless desert.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall to the ground because of weakness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction presents weakness as the cause of falling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become submissive and humble.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense is contrasted with being firm or self-possessed in hardship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect stupidity or dullness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form describes adopting or displaying the manner of a dull person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn over or clap the hands as an expression of grief, sorrow, regret, or perplexity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The gesture is a figurative extension associated with distress; the cited Quran reference in the lexical source is retained only as reported evidence, not converted into a modern verse location.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of dawn or daybreak, to shine or become bright.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an attributed lexical usage recorded as equivalent to تبلّج.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tract serving as an abode or place of resort for animals or jinn, even when it contains no building.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized extension of بلد as a place of habitation rather than necessarily a settled town.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land that has not been dug or upon which fire has not been kindled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage highlights land in an untouched state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A house or dwelling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is reported as a dialectal usage, especially associated with Yemen, and may be grammatically treated like the feminine noun دار.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A burial ground, and according to one report a grave or sepulchre.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence records both the burial-ground sense and the narrower reported sense of an individual grave.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dust or earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a distinct material sense from بلد as a bounded locality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where an ostrich lays and abandons its egg; in idiom, an ostrich egg symbolizes someone isolated, unparalleled, or exposed in the desert.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrase may be used in praise or blame and can describe separation from one's family or relations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trace, mark, or vestige of a dwelling, or a mark remaining upon the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural أبلاد is used for such traces or marks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The origin or an element of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an independently reported, broader lexical extension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression بلدة بيني وبينك, a country or region that separates two people; figuratively, a cause of separation or estrangement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is idiomatic and does not restrict the ordinary land or locality sense of بلدة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert, waterless or desolate tract, and by extension any extensive stretch of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense may describe a place in which one cannot find one's way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mansion of the Moon, or the associated patch or asterism in the sky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical reports identify it with a group of stars in Sagittarius, while recording variant astronomical descriptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hollow or region between the collar-bones, the breast or chest, or the corresponding part of an animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence applies the term to humans, camels, horses, and other animals, with several anatomical specifications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The palm of the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense occurs in a figurative expression for striking one palm against the breast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The form, appearance, or lineaments of the face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is distinct from the narrower space between the eyebrows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stupid, dull, inert, or lacking penetration, vigor, and effectiveness in carrying out affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: أبلد can be the comparative or intensive form; the adjective may also describe softness, weakness, or lack of endurance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stupidity, dullness, or lack of intelligence, penetration, vigor, or effectiveness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the abstract noun corresponding to the quality described by بَلُدَ and بَلِيدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Remaining, staying, abiding, or dwelling in a country or place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is used of one who remains in a بلد or other location.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lasting or not ceasing, failing, or passing away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage is reported as an imitative or paired formation alongside تالد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Large, gross, rude, or coarse in bodily build.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence applies the adjective to a person of a large or coarse make.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Confounded or perplexed, idiotic or deficient in intellect, or unable to proceed when one's means or mount have failed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The several reported applications are treated as related states of confusion, incapacity, or loss of direction.

cautions: بلَد and بَلْدَة overlap in the Quranic land and locality senses; the reported generic-versus-particular distinction is a usage tendency rather than an absolute rule.

Some Lane material is printed under cross-referenced or imperfectly assigned headings such as أَرْضٌ and بيض; it is included here only where the text itself explicitly identifies بلد, بلدة, or a derivative of this root.
The Lane citation connected with the hand-gesture usage uses historical Roman-numeral citation conventions and is not presented as a modern Quran verse location.
